primary_claim: Refusal behavior in small instruction-tuned LLMs is compressed into a single dominant residual-stream direction in some models (Qwen, Gemma, Llama-3.1-8B) but is spread across a low-rank subspace in others (Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Phi-3-mini), so single-direction ablation achieves 80-96% compliance in the former group but only 15-39% in the latter.

effect.metric: compliance rate (LLM-judge, harmful prompts, best single RV)
effect.value: 80-96% for single-direction models (Qwen-1.8B, Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma-2B, Llama-3.1-8B) vs 15-39% for low-rank models (Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3-mini)

contradicts_or_qualifies: The original Arditi et al. single-direction refusal-ablation result does not generalize to all instruction-tuned models; some models require a low-rank subspace rather than a single direction
limitations_stated: LLM-judge evaluation introduces noise, non-determinism, and possible subtle bias
Dataset coverage limited: all harmful/safe prompts generated via DeepSeek's API, so rare cases may be underrepresented
All tested models are under 10B parameters; unclear whether findings generalize to larger models like GPT, Claude, Gemini
quote: For this particular model, refusal is mostly captured by a single, dominant direction in the residual stream.
